title: Screen Reader Accessibility for Unicode Symbols
body:
**Bug Description**
Unicode symbols too noisy for screen reader users

Please add an env var or some config which allows users like myself who are blind programmers to have a cleaner, ascii cli where I can anchor a hotspot on my screen reader to catch the important parts of the cli rather than having to scroll using up or down screen reader keys to read the output.
**Environment Info**
- Platform: macos
- Terminal: iTerm.app
- Version: 0.2.29
- Feedback ID: 828c626a-829f-4565-8364-a0bd0f9eed7b
author: triple7

top_comments.author: sinabahram
top_comments.body: Huge +1 to this with thanks in advance.

top_comments.author: stevemolitor
top_comments.body:
The unicode symbols can also cause issues in certain terminal emulators like [Emacs EAT](https://codeberg.org/akib/emacs-eat), where they can cause layout issues if the font does not contain the unicode character and a fallback font is used.

This also causes issues in Claude Code Emacs wrappers like this [issue](https://github.com/stevemolitor/claude-code.el/issues/1#issuecomment-2727203203) in my claude-code.el package.

There are workarounds, but an option to have a plain ascii CLI would make

top_comments.author: Neurrone
top_comments.body: +1 to this. A related issue: there isn't a way to use + and - to indicate additions / deletions in diffs, and it seems to only be indicated by colour.
